title: Suppress transient throttle credits and reconcile delayed usage backfills
creator: Priya Nair
description: Summary: We are seeing bursts of transient rate-limit (HTTP 429) events that trigger automated rate-limit credit issuance and downstream invoice line generation. When the 429s are short-lived or caused by client retry storms, credits are applied, but later backfills of usage (delayed webhook/retry arrivals) or dedup runs cause the credits to become incorrect, producing either duplicate credit lines or negative net adjustments on invoices. This ticket implements suppression and reconciliation logic to reduce noise from transient throttle storms and ensure idempotent, auditable export lines to Stripe/NetSuite.
proposed_solution: 1) Add a suppression window (hysteresis) to the rate-limit crediter: do not create a credit unless the same customer experiences sustained 429s above threshold for a rolling 10-minute window. 2) Mark provisional credits as 'pending' in the internal ledger and avoid exporting pending credits to Stripe until the window closes or a manual confirmation occurs. 3) When backfilled usage arrives, re-evaluate pending credits and either finalize, reduce, or cancel them deterministically. 4) Improve export deduplication keys by including credit provenance (suppress-window-id + aggregated-interval) to prevent duplicate Stripe line items when reconciler runs overlap. 5) Add reconciler job to detect and remediate stale pending credits older than 7 days and surface for manual review.
acceptance_criteria: No new transient-throttle credit exports for customers where 429 spike lasted < 10 minutes (verified in staging)
Exported credit lines include provenance metadata (suppress-window-id) in the memo/metadata field
Reconciler run can identify pending credits and re-evaluate them after backfill with deterministic outcome: finalize/adjust/cancel
Automated tests for suppression window and export dedupe added with >95% coverage for new logic
Monitoring: rate of duplicate credit exports decreased by >=90% for recent incidents during canary rollout
Concourse job for idempotent export passes on canary tenant and secondary region
implementation_plan: Design: update crediter service to introduce pending state and suppression window (backend change) — Priya
DB: add columns credit.pending boolean, credit.suppress_window_id (string), credit.created_window_ts (timestamp) — DB migration by DB eng
Export: change export pipeline to filter pending credits unless the credit.finalized=true or pending age > 7d with review flag
Reconciler: implement backfill re-evaluation job that recalculates net credit given new usage and writes adjustment actions (finalize/adjust/cancel)
API/Exports: include suppress_window_id and original_event_count as export metadata fields when writing Stripe line_item metadata
QA: create synthetic 429 storm and backfill test harness in staging, run reconciliation scenarios
Rollout: feature flag behind 'suppress-transient-throttle-credits' — enable for 10% of tenants, evaluate metrics, then ramp
Docs: update billing runbook and Confluence page explaining pending credit lifecycle and manual remediation steps
rollout_plan: Phase 0: deploy DB migration and feature-gated code to staging. Run synthetic tests (QA team)
Phase 1: Canary - enable feature for internal and selected sandbox customers (10%) for 48h, monitor duplicate-credit-export metric and invoice deltas
Phase 2: Ramp to 50% tenants over 5 days, continue monitoring and run reconciliation job daily
Phase 3: Full rollout after 2 weeks of stable metrics and audit of 5 sample reconciliations

Rollback: if duplicate export rate or customer invoice variance increases >1% absolute or manual remediation workload spikes, flip feature flag off and run emergency reconciler to revert pending credits
testing_plan: Unit tests for suppression window logic and pending->finalize transition
Integration test: simulate retry storm (burst of 429s) and short backfill to assert pending credits are not exported
E2E test with Stripe sandbox: create provisional credit and verify metadata appears only on final exported credits
Load test: ensure suppression tracking scales under 10k concurrent customer throttle events
Chaos test: force delayed webhook replay and ensure reconciler produces deterministic adjustments
monitoring_diagnostics: New Prometheus gauge: billing.credits.pending_count by tenant and region
New counter: billing.exports.duplicate_credit_attempts (alert if >10 in 1h on prod)
Dashboards: 'Throttle credit lifecycle' showing 429 rate, pending->finalized ratio, backfill-triggered adjustments
SLOs to watch: invoice_net_change_pct (expect <0.5% variance after rollout), duplicate_export_rate target <0.1%
Runbook steps: how to query pending credits, re-run reconciler, and create manual reversal in Netsuite
notes: Trade-offs: Suppression window reduces noisy credits but increases time before some legitimate credits appear on invoices; choose 10m as a balance based on historical 429 duration percentiles
We considered an immediate idempotent credit with negative export signature, but Stripe invoice UX made this confusing for customers. Using pending state keeps invoices clean and auditable
Edge case: customers with frequent sustained 429s still need prompt credits; suppression only suppresses short spikes and will finalize when threshold crossed
Operational burden: adds pending state that requires housekeeping; reconciler cleans stale entries and flags for finance team review
